doc.title: Marty Morell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Playing behind or on the beat; the Ellington feel
summary: Finding where the music grooves, with the laid back Ellington band feel.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Is there such a thing as playing behind the beat or ahead of the beat?

Well you hear that a lot. I think the main thing is finding where it grooves. Where is feels best. You know, and certain tunes, you know, like in the Ellington band, right, I had the good fortune to work with the Ellington band for about six years, six and a half years. And you know it’s a more laid back kind of feel, like especially like something like “Jeep’s Blues” or even “Satin Doll” with that band – it’s laid back but it really grooves. And it’s not really behind the beat but it’s just in a place where it really feels good, right? And then it depends on the tempo. I mean you’re not going to lay back if you’re playing an uptempo. You know what I mean? It’s the tempo that’s pushing you forward so you’ve got to keep driving it, right? But certain kinds of music lend themselves to a little bit more laid back style, right? And that’s kind of how I approach it. But basically you just try to get it feeling good, wherever it sits. And that’s the place I try to get to, every time I play.
